findings.text: follow-on: _cited_absolute_paths treats every absolute path token in the manifest as an owned arm, so a directory the manifest merely mentions under the temp root - in prose or an example command rather than as a test arm - is a removal candidate; the protections (repository, worktree, run directory, live-run citations) bound the reach, but the done_when reaches only what the manifest cites 'as a test arm, basetemp or control tree'.

follow-on: remove_cited_arms runs inside _release_run_workspace, which _release_after_promotion also calls for blocked and failed gates with release_worktree=False, so a blocked run's cited arms are removed although the done_when scopes the clearing to a run whose gate passed; the cited logs are copied first, so the log evidence survives.

follow-on: the evidence fragment carries no figure although the node declared a figures directory, and a small diagram of the removal reach (temp-root bound, protections, live-run citations) would communicate the bounded removal the text describes in prose.
